newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury welcomes news of IMF Thailand talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury welcomes news of IMF Thailand talks.

text.p: The United States will follow talks between Thailand and the International Monetary Fund closely, but sees the start of discussions as "a constructive step," a senior Treasury official said Monday.
"We welcome the dialogue between Thailand and the International Monetary Fund as a constructive step and will be following it closely," Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said in a statement.
"The United States has a strong stake in financial stability and growth throughout the developing world," Summers added.

Thai officials said earlier on Monday that Bangkok was discussing the possibility of borrowing money from the IMF to overcome a financial crisis and ease liquidity problems. Such a loan would mean Thailand meeting tough IMF conditions.
An IMF spokesman said a team from the fund had already arrived in Bangkok. "An IMF team arrived in Thailand over the weekend and has initiated policy discussions with Thai officials," he said.

Thailand, bowing to strong speculative pressure, floated the baht currency earlier this month. But officials had said they had no intention of seeking IMF aid, which could open the door to bilateral funding from neighbors such as Japan.
